name: Maple Finance / Orthogonal Trading default (FTX contagion, Nov–Dec 2022)
speed: Jump-to-default: ~4 weeks of concealed insolvency with zero on-chain signal, then an instantaneous ~80% pool markdown on the day of the default notice (2022-12-05). MPL token: −24.7% in 24h, ~−58% to the December low. Contrast with market-crash events: no drawdown path to react to — the entire loss materialized in one announcement.
summary: Дефолт Orthogonal Trading в Maple M11 (ноя-дек 2022): фонд ~4 недели СКРЫВАЛ потери на FTX (говорил делегату про $2.5M экспозиции), продолжая быть должным пулам, и 05.12.2022 объявлен дефолт на $36M (8 займов) — $31M из ~$38.5M активных займов пула M11 USDC (~80% мгновенной уценки капитала кредиторов). Сигнала на цепочке НЕ БЫЛО: APY и TVL пула выглядели здоровыми до самого объявления, а локапы Maple 1.0 (90 дней + 10-дневный cooldown) делали выход невозможным даже после тревожного звонка Auros 30.11. Финальный возврат кредиторам публично НЕ закрыт (подтверждено лишь ~$2.5M near-term recovery). Флагманский стресс нашего кредитного рукава. Книга SPA на 2026-08: aave_v3 40% / pendle (PT_USDC) 20% / maple 15% / morpho_steakhouse 15% / кэш USDC 10%.

timeline.event: FTX halts customer withdrawals as Alameda/FTX crisis breaks; Orthogonal Trading has substantial funds on the exchange
FTX files Chapter 11. Start of the concealment window: through November, Orthogonal repeatedly tells pool delegate M11 Credit its FTX exposure is only ~$2.5M

First public crack (different borrower, same delegate): Auros Global misses a principal payment on a 2,400 wETH (~$3M) loan in the M11 wETH pool; 5-day grace period starts. Maple pool APYs otherwise look healthy — no on-chain signal of Orthogonal's condition
MPL prints December 2022 low ~$2.94 (~−58% from pre-default ~$7, ~−88% from Aug 2022 high ~$24)
Orthogonal Trading reverses its story: discloses to M11 Credit that FTX losses are substantially larger than the claimed $2.5M and that it cannot repay its loans (effectively insolvent for ~4 weeks)

M11 Credit issues notice of default on all 8 Orthogonal loans: $36M total — $31M in the M11 USDC pool (~80% of its ~$38.5M active loans) and ~$5M in the M11 wETH pool (~17% hit); ~30% of all active Maple loans. Maple severs all ties with Orthogonal Trading (borrower) and Orthogonal Credit (delegate); expected near-term recovery only ~$2.5M (pool cover + accrued fees)

MPL token −24.7% in 24h to $5.29 (CoinGecko via The Block); lenders cannot exit — Maple 1.0 requires deposit lockup (30-90d per source) then a 10-day cooldown plus ~2-day withdrawal window, and pool cash is far below queued withdrawals
Bloomberg/CoinDesk confirm default as FTX contagion; reports of internal dissent at Orthogonal; Maple community weighs response
CoinDesk tallies ~$54M of soured debt (Orthogonal + Auros) = ~66% of Maple's $82M total outstanding loans across its four active pools

Maple 2.0 released: request-based prorated/scheduled withdrawals, delegate-declared immediate defaults with instant loss recognition, mandatory delegate first-loss capital, auto-compounding; Solana lending discontinued
Auros Global discloses it is in provisional liquidation (BVI) while negotiating with creditors
Orthogonal Trading placed under provisional liquidation by BVI court on petition of M11 Credit + Maple Foundation; Kroll appointed as Joint Provisional Liquidators
Kroll representatives appointed full Joint Liquidators of Orthogonal Trading (late Jan); recovery bottleneck: information from the FTX estate (Orthogonal's main asset is its FTX claim)
Auros restructures its ~$18M M11-pool debt: 55% repaid immediately, 40% reissued ≤9 months at 8.64%, 5% ≤90 days at 0%
M11 Credit confirms 100% repayment of Auros loans secured. Orthogonal side remains in liquidation with no published final distribution to M11 USDC pool lenders

maple_protocol.m11_usdc_pool: Orthogonal owed $31M of ~$38.5M active loans (~80%); remaining lenders faced ~80% loss on capital at default; expected near-term offset only ~$2.5M (pool cover + Orthogonal's accrued platform fees)
maple_protocol.m11_weth_pool: ~$5M of Orthogonal debt in default (~17% pool hit); same pool also carried Auros's 8,400 wETH (~$10.7M) distressed exposure

maple_protocol.governance_response: Maple severed all ties with Orthogonal (borrower) and Orthogonal Credit (delegate) on 2022-12-05 and shut its pools; Maple 2.0 shipped 2022-12-14: modular contracts, request-based prorated/scheduled withdrawals (replacing deposit lockup + 10-day cooldown), delegate-declared instant defaults with immediate loss recognition, mandatory delegate first-loss capital, auto-compounding, Solana lending discontinued

defi_impact.no_onchain_signal: KEY LESSON (confirmed): a private-credit borrower default has no on-chain price signal beforehand. Pool APY and TVL looked healthy until the 2022-12-05 announcement; the only public warning was Auros missing a wETH principal payment on 2022-11-30 — five days earlier and about a different borrower — and Maple 1.0's lockup/cooldown withdrawal design meant even lenders who reacted to it could not exit. Loss arrived as an instantaneous jump-to-default markdown, not a tradeable drawdown path.
defi_impact.composability: Damage stayed inside Maple's credit pools: no oracle failure, no exploit, no liquidation cascade into overcollateralized DeFi (Aave/Compound/Morpho-style markets unaffected); USDC itself never depegged. This is idiosyncratic counterparty credit risk wearing a DeFi wrapper.
defi_impact.sector_effect: Uncollateralized on-chain credit sector (Maple, TrueFi, Clearpool) lost depositor trust; Maple's outstanding loans had already fallen from a ~$900M-scale 2022 peak to $82M by mid-Dec 2022.

causes.root_cause: Uncollateralized (private-credit) DeFi lending: Orthogonal Trading, a crypto hedge fund borrowing from Maple Finance's M11 Credit-managed pools, had large funds trapped on FTX when it collapsed (Chapter 11 filed 2022-11-11). Orthogonal concealed the loss — during November 2022 it repeatedly told pool delegate M11 Credit its FTX exposure was only ~$2.5M — and kept operating 'while effectively insolvent' for ~4 weeks before admitting on 2022-12-03 that it could not repay.
causes.mechanism: Maple 1.0 loans were under-collateralized loans to whitelisted institutional borrowers, underwritten off-chain by pool delegates (M11 Credit / Orthogonal Credit). There was no on-chain collateral to liquidate and no on-chain price signal of borrower distress: the pools' APY and TVL looked healthy until the default notice. When M11 Credit declared default on 2022-12-05, the loss was marked against lenders' pool shares instantly (jump-to-default), with no drawdown path in between.
aggravating_factors: Pool delegate due diligence failed: Orthogonal's own affiliate (Orthogonal Credit) was simultaneously a Maple pool delegate, and delegates accepted borrower self-reported financials
Concentration: Orthogonal's $31M was ~80% of the M11 USDC pool's ~$38.5M of active loans; the $36M default was ~30% of ALL active loans on Maple

Maple 1.0 withdrawal mechanics (deposit lockup, reported as 90-day per protocol docs / 'minimum 30 days' per Cointelegraph, then a 10-day cooldown plus ~2-day exit window) plus pools being nearly fully lent meant lenders could not exit even after the 2022-11-30 Auros warning sign
'Pool cover' first-loss reserves were tiny relative to loans (~$2.5M expected recovery vs $36M default)
FTX contagion hit multiple Maple borrowers at once (Orthogonal, Auros), so soured debt reached ~66% of the $82M outstanding across Maple's four active pools by 2022-12-12
causes.prior_context: Maple had already taken its first credit loss in July 2022: Babel Finance defaulted on a $10M USDC loan in the Orthogonal Credit-delegated pool (notice of default 2022-07-01, liquidated 2022-07-10), lenders booked a $7.9M loss = ~3.2% haircut on ~$244M pool deposits — an early demonstration of the same no-collateral, no-on-chain-signal failure mode.

contagion: FTX/Alameda collapse (2022-11-08/11) → Orthogonal Trading (BVI hedge fund) funds trapped on FTX
Orthogonal conceals insolvency ~4 weeks while continuing to owe Maple M11 pools → default notice 2022-12-05 on $36M (8 loans)
M11 USDC pool: $31M of ~$38.5M active loans in default (~80% pool hit); M11 wETH pool: ~$5M (~17% hit)
Parallel FTX casualty: Auros Global misses 2,400 wETH (~$3M) principal payment 2022-11-30; total Auros debt ~$18M to M11 pools; provisional liquidation disclosed 2022-12-20
Protocol level: soured debt ~$54M = ~66% of Maple's $82M outstanding loans by 2022-12-12; MPL token −24.7% in a day, ~−58% to December low ~$2.94
Corporate unwind: Orthogonal placed in BVI provisional liquidation 2022-12-22 (Kroll), full Joint Liquidators late Jan 2023
Trust contagion to the uncollateralized-credit sector broadly (TrueFi/Clearpool peers repriced; Maple deposits fled), forcing the Maple 2.0 redesign (2022-12-14)
NOT propagated: no stablecoin depeg, no smart-contract exploit, no cascade into overcollateralized money markets (Aave/Compound unaffected)

recovery.near_term: ~$2.5M expected recovery for M11 USDC pool lenders from pool cover + Orthogonal's accrued platform fees (vs $36M default) — announced 2022-12-05/06.
recovery.orthogonal_liquidation: BVI court placed Orthogonal Trading in provisional liquidation ~2022-12-22 with Kroll as Joint Provisional Liquidators (petitioned by M11 Credit + Maple Foundation); Kroll appointed full Joint Liquidators late January 2023. Main recoverable asset was Orthogonal's claim on the FTX estate; M11's status updates named lack of FTX-estate information as the bottleneck. No final creditor distribution percentage has been published — final LGD for M11 USDC lenders remains publicly unresolved (FTX estate's 2024-25 cash distributions at >100% of petition-date values likely improved it, but no confirmation).
recovery.auros_contrast: The parallel Auros exposure (~$18M to M11 pools) resolved far better: restructuring agreed 2023-02-15 (55% repaid immediately, 40% reissued ≤9 months at 8.64%, 5% ≤90 days at 0%); M11 Credit confirmed 100% repayment secured by 2023-11-08 (~11 months).
recovery.protocol_recovery: Maple 2.0 (2022-12-14) rebuilt withdrawals, default handling and delegate first-loss capital; Maple survived, pivoted toward collateralized/RWA lending through 2023 and TVL later recovered to multi-billion scale (2024-25), but Maple 1.0-style unsecured pools were effectively abandoned.
recovery.time_to_partial_recovery: Pool cover distribution: weeks. Auros side: 55% in ~2.5 months, 100% in ~11 months. Orthogonal side: >1 year, final amount unknown.

confidence_notes: Headline numbers ($36M / 8 loans / $31M in M11 USDC pool / ~80% pool loss / ~30% of Maple's active loans / Dec 5 2022 default notice) are confirmed by 3+ independent outlets (The Block, CoinDesk, Bloomberg, Decrypt). Corrections to the brief: concealment was ~4 weeks (FTX Ch.11 Nov 11 → disclosure Dec 3, and M11's own '4 weeks' language), not ~5; wETH-pool exposure was ~$5M (~17% pool hit), confirmed. Maple 1.0 withdrawal terms are the weakest area: protocol docs-derived sources describe a 90-day deposit lockup then 10-day cooldown + ~2-day exit window, while Cointelegraph's Maple 2.0 coverage says 'minimum of 30 days to withdraw after deposit' — I report the range; either way exit before default was impossible. MPL intraday figures: −24.7% to $5.29 on Dec 5 (The Block, CoinGecko-sourced) is solid; the December 2022 low ~$2.94 comes from aggregator historical data (CoinLore/Bitget) — medium confidence; pre-default reference ~$7.0 is back-computed from The Block's −24.7% and marked accordingly. Final loss-given-default for M11 USDC lenders is UNRESOLVED publicly: only ~$2.5M near-term recovery (pool cover + accrued fees) was confirmed, Kroll's BVI liquidation of Orthogonal (main asset: an FTX estate claim) has no published final distribution — reported as null rather than estimated. FTX actual-exposure size for Orthogonal was never publicly quantified beyond 'substantially larger than $2.5M' — null. Auros full repayment by 2023-11-08 is from M11 Credit's own Medium post (single primary source, but consistent with CoinDesk's Feb 2023 restructuring terms).

data_availability.onchain: Full Ethereum history of Maple v1 pool contracts (deposits, loan drawdowns, default/liquidation txs) is public; Maple subgraph and Dune dashboards cover pool balances. Crucially, on-chain APY/TVL series show NO pre-default distress — useful as a negative control for signal research.

book_mapping.maple_15pct: DIRECT HIT — this event is the historical stress case for the $15,000 Maple sleeve. If that sleeve had sat in the affected M11 USDC pool: ~80% instantaneous markdown = −$12,000 = −12.0% of the $100k book in one block, with the position locked (no exit possible). Even a protocol-average outcome (~66% of outstanding loans soured, LGD uncertain) implies high-single-digit to ~10% book loss from a 15% sleeve.
book_mapping.aave_v3_40pct: Unaffected in the historical event — overcollateralized money markets saw no contagion from Maple's credit loss. Aave's risk is a different class (oracle/liquidation/utilization), not borrower credit.
book_mapping.pendle_pt_20pct: No direct analog (Pendle PT is overcollateralized yield-splitting). Partial analogy on exit liquidity only: PT sold pre-maturity in a panic takes a discount, but there is a market — unlike Maple 1.0 where exit was structurally impossible.
book_mapping.morpho_steakhouse_15pct: Did not exist in Dec 2022. Steakhouse USDC lends against on-chain collateral, so borrower jump-to-default in this form doesn't apply; the transferable lesson is curator risk (delegate ≈ curator: an agent whose off-chain judgment you cannot verify from chain data).

spa_relevance.kill_switch_implication: CRITICAL: this event defeats the two-tier drawdown ladder. Loss arrives as a single-block jump-to-default (−12% of book from the Maple sleeve alone), skipping straight past SOFT_DERISK (−5%) into HARD_KILL (≥−10%) territory with zero time to de-risk — and HARD_KILL's 'all-cash' response cannot liquidate a defaulted, locked credit position anyway. Drawdown-reactive controls are ex-post here; the only effective control is ex-ante sizing.
risk_policy_gaps_exposed: APY/TVL-based gates are blind to private-credit counterparty risk: M11 USDC pool (~$38.5M active loans) passes the $5M TVL floor, APY looked healthy until the announcement, and live-TVL checks (ADR-053) would have shown nothing wrong on Dec 4

Withdrawal terms must be a first-class risk parameter: Maple 1.0's deposit lockup (30-90d) + 10-day cooldown + ~2-day window means 'DERISK всегда быстро' is physically impossible — fail-CLOSED cannot execute on locked capital

Per-protocol cap is the only defense that works: with 80% LGD, keeping worst-case single-protocol loss under the 10% HARD_KILL budget requires the uncollateralized-credit sleeve ≤12.5% (current 15% Maple weight implies a 12% worst-case hit)

The one observable early signal (Auros missing a wETH payment on 2022-11-30, T-5 days, different borrower, same delegate) argues for a delegate/curator-level contagion rule: any missed payment in a delegate's pool family ⇒ freeze new allocation to ALL that delegate's pools (cap-at-held, fail-CLOSED)
spa_relevance.stress_test_spec: Model as jump process, not path: at T0 mark Maple sleeve −80% (severe, historical M11 USDC) / −17% (moderate, wETH-pool analog) / −3.2% (mild, Babel 2022 analog) with recovery lag of 12+ months and recovered fraction uncertain (use 0-30% of loss for severe case); no exit possible for locked sleeve regardless of warning; other sleeves flat; MPL-style governance-token hedge assumption invalid (−25% day one, −58% to trough).

assumptions: maple −80% день 27 (05.12.2022) — уценка капитала кредиторов пула M11 USDC при дефолте ($31M из ~$38.5M), подтверждена 3+ источниками; финальный LGD публично не закрыт — берём уценку на дату дефолта.
freeze весь горизонт — локапы Maple 1.0 по построению (90д + cooldown): выход был невозможен и ДО дефолта.
H07 (FTX) моделирует тот же арк с диверсифицированным допущением −30%; здесь — концентрированная реальность одного пула. Не суммировать.
